intro_html: A tagine is a slow braise built on warm spice instead of heat, and this one leans on cumin, turmeric, paprika, and cinnamon with golden raisins for sweetness and a squeeze of lemon to cut it. The chickpeas are the budget trick. They stretch the beef, add their own protein, and soak up the sauce. Each bowl runs 681 calories and 55 grams of protein for about $7.04 a serving (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $7.04 a bowl (at everyday cost). The beef is nearly the whole number, which means the chickpeas, carrots, and canned tomatoes are essentially riding along for free while doing half the work of filling the container.
shop_smart: Chickpeas are the reason this dish is affordable at all. They carry bulk and protein for a fraction of what beef costs per pound, so never think of them as filler. They are the strategy.
Chuck roast dominates the receipt. Buy it when it is marked down and freeze it in batch-sized chunks, because that single decision moves this recipe more than every other line combined.

The spice rack does the heavy flavor lifting here, and jars you already own cost you nothing extra tonight. If you are buying fresh, buy whole containers of cumin and turmeric rather than the little bottles, since the per-ounce price is much better.
Golden raisins seem fussy but a small amount goes a long way, and one bag survives many batches. They are what makes a tagine taste like a tagine instead of a beef stew with cumin in it.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into large cubes, pat dry, season with salt and pepper, and brown in batches in a heavy pot. Set the meat aside and leave the browned bits in the pot.
Cook the sliced red onion until soft, then add the garlic and ginger and stir for a minute until you can smell them.
Add the cumin, turmeric, paprika, and cinnamon and toast them in the oil for about 30 seconds. Blooming dry spices in fat is what separates a tagine from a bowl of dusty stew.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the diced tomatoes and beef broth, scraping the bottom clean. Return the beef with the bay leaves.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the beef pulls apart under a fork.
Add the carrots, drained chickpeas, brown sugar, and golden raisins and simmer uncovered another 30 minutes so the sauce thickens and the carrots go tender.
Finish off the heat with the lemon juice and a big handful of chopped cilantro. The acid at the end wakes the whole pot up.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14 for your gram target. Weigh each container instead of ladling by eye, because the beef sinks and the person who scoops last gets robbed. Every portion lands at 681 calories that way.

steps: Season and brown the beef cubes in batches, then set aside.
Soften the red onion, add garlic and ginger, then toast the dry spices in the oil.
Stir in tomato paste, diced tomatoes, and beef broth, then return the beef and simmer covered about 2 hours.
Add carrots, chickpeas, brown sugar, and raisins and simmer uncovered 30 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro, then weigh and divide into 14 containers.
